messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Help with DS submodel in MRDS
parts:
Thanks for your question and welcome to the group.

The first step in diagnosing the problem is determining which model generates the error. From your partial output, I'm guessing the ~distance+VegClass model caused the problem. To be sure, run that model alone (without the loop).

If that is the problematic model, next is the question of why. My suspicion is there is insufficient detections to support the fit of that model. I would diagnose this by determining the number of detections within each of the categories of VegClass. Your model is asking that a detection function be fitted for each VegClass category; I suspect that might be creating a numerical problem for the software.

If the software is struggling with the model that includes only~distance+VegClass then those problems will likely persist (indeed magnify) when you try to fit even more complex models that include VegClass.

parts:
Jess

Glad you found your difficulties with VegClass. Also good you are double-checking the output from your analysis. The double-check is always important because MRDS is describing how it thinks the data were collected, i.e., the survey design.

The "k" in the summary statistics table you show is the number of physical transects visited. I don't know about your design but few surveys have 100+ transects in each stratum. If transects are visited more than once, they should not be considered separate spatial replicates, but rather the effort associated with the transect would be its physical length multiplied by the number of visits.

Thanks for your question and welcome to the group.

The first step in diagnosing the problem is determining which model generates the error. From your partial output, I'm guessing the ~distance+VegClass model caused the problem. To be sure, run that model alone (without the loop).

If that is the problematic model, next is the question of why. My suspicion is there is insufficient detections to support the fit of that model. I would diagnose this by determining the number of detections within each of the categories of VegClass. Your model is asking that a detection function be fitted for each VegClass category; I suspect that might be creating a numerical problem for the software.

If the software is struggling with the model that includes only~distance+VegClass then those problems will likely persist (indeed magnify) when you try to fit even more complex models that include VegClass.
